novelty_flags.one_line: The table calls ChenHuang2025, SmuclerLanniMasip2025, and RudolphVanderLaan2017 “strict_tightening,” but no statement gives a strict class inclusion, rate comparison, or iff frontier against any of their published results.

soundness_flags.label: target estimand, ass:outcome-transport, ass:receipt-transport, and prop:compact-causal-range
soundness_flags.one_line: P_T is only a law of X, so the target reduced forms are not defined by the model and the target CACE has no target potential-outcome/IV law; define a target full-data law and its reduced forms, or state the target solely as the transported observed-law functional.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:unknown-weight-attainment
soundness_flags.one_line: The question quantifies “one C∈𝔠cell” although 𝔠cell contains sequences (C_n), and then evaluates C_n; quantify one sequence (C_n) instead.

soundness_flags.label: ass:outcome-transport and ass:receipt-transport
soundness_flags.one_line: These conditions are tagged standard and cited to ChenHuang2025, but that paper assumes conditional transport of the treatment-effect contrast and an integrated target-covariate first-stage equality, not pointwise equality of target and source observed reduced forms.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2, Assumption 2, lines 129–134; Section 3, Assumption 4 and Theorem 3.1, lines 170–189
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines a target population with only X observed, assumes conditional equality of treatment-effect contrasts and an integrated target-X first-stage equality, and identifies T-CACE through its displayed target-weighted Wald formula.
The paper studies single-population score-test inversion for LATE, uniform validity with arbitrarily weak instruments, six set shapes, and possible infinite diameter.
The paper studies identification-robust LATE inference with high-dimensional covariates and an orthogonalized Anderson–Rubin test, without a transport population.

source_verification_receipts.version: author manuscript corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 157 (2010), pp. 236–247; publisher primary text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs weak-IV-robust confidence sets by test inversion and explicitly discusses expected length as an accuracy criterion in the linear-IV setting.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv manuscript corresponding to Econometrica 89 (2021), pp. 1141–1177; journal metadata confirmed
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper concerns finite-sample optimal ATE estimation and confidence intervals under unconfoundedness with smoothness/shape restrictions and limited overlap, rather than a weak-IV ratio.

source_verification_receipts.version: JRSS-B 79(5) (2017), pp. 1509–1525; publisher full text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops TMLEs for transported ITT, complier ATE, and exposure effects in encouragement designs, including discussion of practical positivity violations.
The paper studies regular doubly robust transport/generalization estimation of target ATEs, convergence rates, limiting distributions, efficiency, and minimax results.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a full target potential-outcome/encouragement law and state the exact population-level IV and transport assumptions needed for the source weighted ratio to equal target CACE; alternatively retitle the estimand as a transported reduced-form ratio.

Replace the “strict_tightening” comparator-table entries with “informed_by,” or formulate an explicit strict extension statement that nests each cited regular model and identifies the weak/overlap regime it newly covers.

Make the rate claim maximally diagnostic by additively testing the retained fourth seed: construct two nondegenerate admissible weight geometries with the same t_n, or prove a lemma showing the envelope makes higher moments irrelevant.

recommended_next_step: Revise the target-law/transport specification and comparator framing, then retain the field-tier minimax frontier for Stage 0.
